title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Handling Charge on a Month's Arrears Fee
content:
| Invoices that fell due within the window | What the payments received in it leave standing | The open position | The handling charge added |
|---|---|---|---|
| two or more | part of the invoiced total standing | above the tier's credit limit | 80 US dollars, being twice the charge of 40 US dollars |
| two or more | part of the invoiced total standing | at or below the tier's credit limit | 40 US dollars |
| two or more | nothing standing | any | no handling charge is added |
| fewer than two | any | any | no handling charge is added |

The window is the 12 months to the day the fee is raised, and the open position is what the program
invoiced in that window less what was received in it.

The credit limit the third column is measured against, by program under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Credit limit (USD) |
|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 7500 |
| Priority Response Program | 15000 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 25000 |
| Emergency Response Program | 40000 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 75000 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 150000 |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A rate program on the Priority Response Program, whose credit limit is
15000 US dollars, carries three invoices that fell due inside the window and payments leaving part of
the invoiced total standing. Where the open position is 16000 US dollars the handling charge is 80 US
dollars; where it is 9000 US dollars the handling charge is 40 US dollars. A program carrying a single
invoice that fell due in the window carries no handling charge whatever the open position.
